data.narrative:
Dragonfly Aerospace is a Series G-stage space and aerospace company founded by Bryan Dean that has raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage companies including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though tight filtering constraints limit applicability of certain methods.

Of three potential valuation approaches, only stage-progression methodology is sufficiently supported by available data. Using total capital raised ($20M) as a base proxy and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement yields an implied valuation of $51M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied absent the target's disclosed revenue; while the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 23.9x revenues across the five public comparables, private company revenue figures are not on file. Peer-median analysis similarly cannot support a tight conclusion, as fewer than three same-stage or adjacent-stage private peers meet filtering thresholds, making sector-wide medians unreliable proxies for a frontier-stage company.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $44M to $59M, centered on $51M. This range reflects uncertainty around capital efficiency and stage-specific multiples; the actual valuation should be stress-tested against capital deployment milestones and runway profile, neither of which appear in current data. Revenue trajectory and customer concentration represent material blind spots pending disclosure.
